rule: A clock string is hh:mm, 00:00 through 23:59, and where 00:00 appears decides what it means: as an end it is the end of the Day, 1440 minutes in; as a start it is the beginning of the Day, 0 minutes in. A range is half-open, [start, end), so it occupies time only when endMinutes is greater than startMinutes. 24:00 is never a clock string; 1440 is only ever a number.
why: core and web each read this clock, and web never imports core, so the rule is necessarily written twice. This table is the one place it is written down, so that a change to either reading fails a test instead of drifting quietly (issue #48).
notCovered: Every case here is zero-padded, because zero-padded is the only thing either side reads: issue #54 narrowed core to the pattern the schemas and web already carried, so an unpadded "9:00" is refused by both and there is no difference left for the table to state. No unpadded row was added for that reason. Refusals cannot be a row in any case — a case is two numbers and cannot say "no time at all" — so each side pins its own, core/src/clock.test.ts and web/src/timetable/week.test.ts. Nor does the table cover the writing back of minutes as a clock string, which only web does.

cases.why: an ordinary morning, and the shape every other case is judged against
the evening, run to the end of the Day: an end of 00:00 is 1440, not 0
the night, and only the night: a start of 00:00 is 0, not 1440
the whole Day, read positionally from both ends of the same spelling
the Day's last hour, the half a night shift that is not the next Day's
the Day's last minute, which is a minute and not nothing
the other half of that night shift, on its own Day
occupies no time: an end that does not advance past its start, and neither is 00:00
occupies no time: a range lies within the one Day it names and never wraps past midnight
occupies no time: plainly backwards, and read as written rather than repaired
